judged_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:349 — in createAllCalendarEvents, when `this.calendarCredentials.find((c) => c.id === destination.credentialId)` misses, the code falls back to `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: destination.credentialId } })` with no check that the credential's userId/teamId belongs to this booking's organizer/team, so a credentialId that ends up in a destinationCalendar record no longer resolves only from the pre-scoped `calendarCredentials` set and could be used to create a calendar event with any credential row in the DB; confidence 50 (exploitability depends on whether credentialId in destinationCalendar can ever diverge from a legitimately-related host, which this diff does not itself demonstrate) — severity P2.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that `createAllCalendarEvents` now falls back to fetching an arbitrary credential by `destination.credentialId` from the DB (`prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: destination.credentialId } })`) when it is not present in the pre-scoped `this.calendarCredentials`, and then uses it to call `createEvent`. There is no verification in this new fallback that the fetched credential belongs to the organizer/user/team context of the event, so the function can act on a credential row outside the originally scoped credential set if a `destinationCalendar` contains an unexpected `credentialId`.
